newsitem.title: USA: Pronet says Lehman sues over court expenses.
newsitem.headline: Pronet says Lehman sues over court expenses.

text.p: ProNet Inc, a paging company, said Thursday it was sued by Lehman Bros., the lead underwriter in a stock offering in 1996.
It said Lehman is seeking indemnification and recovery of legal costs to defend certain lawsuits filed against ProNet and its underwriters.
ProNet said Lehman filed the suit on behalf of the underwriting syndicate for the offering and was seeking class action status for the case.
ProNet said it was reviewing Lehman's complaint and evaluating defenses and and counterclaims. It said it intends to defend vigorously against Lehman's allegations.
On May 16, ProNet announced that it and its insurance carriers had agreed to pay $5 million to settle a group of class-action suits against the company, its officers and directors.

The suits were filed after the price of the company's stock plunged in June last year. The plaintiffs alleged that the company and others schemed to inflate the price of its stock so it can make acquisitions.
The settlement did not resolve claims against underwriters in the offering or any potential claims that the underwriters may bring against the company.
However, the proposed settlement limits ProNet's liability for underwriter claims to $6.5 million, plus attorneys' fees.
